pinned_source.title: Random Planted 3-SAT
pinned_source.author: Encyclopedia of Algorithms chapter; Feige and Vilenchik technical report for k-OPT details
pinned_source.license: No source-code license asserted; clean-room algorithm implementation

input.encoding: [n,m,3*m signed one-based literals grouped by clause]

contract.formula: Every 3-CNF clause has three nonzero signed variable IDs with distinct variables.
contract.initial_assignment: Majority Vote; positive polarity wins only when its count is strictly greater; ties and unseen variables are false.
contract.improving_move: Flip between one and k variables and strictly enlarge the set of satisfied clause positions: retain every currently satisfied clause and satisfy at least one formerly unsatisfied clause.
contract.search: For each k starting at 1, enumerate complete assignments in lexicographic order (variable 1 first, false before true). Select the first assignment at Hamming distance 1..k that is an improving move. Repeat at that k until no move exists, then increase k and continue from the current assignment.
contract.termination: A satisfying assignment yields status 1. If no improvement exists at k=n, return status 0 and the current assignment; at that radius every assignment is considered, so no satisfying assignment exists.
contract.output: [status,assignment[0..n)] as signed-i64 words; status is 1 or 0 and each assignment word is 1=true or -1=false.
contract.profile_scope: The source leaves arbitration among improving moves unspecified; lexicographic assignment order fixes this choice. Direct exhaustive enumeration is bounded to n<=12 and realizes the paper's set-based move semantics; it does not implement the paper's depth-k search-tree speedup or its probabilistic guarantee.

workspace.meaning: Fixed clause, assignment, polarity-count, and staged-output storage for n<=12 and m<=32.
